archetypes.name: launcher-contracts
archetypes.rationale: The plan introduces a generic launcher whose sidecar, retry, exit, and collector contracts must align with existing external-agent mechanics.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit whether the proposed launch-codex-exec.sh behavior matches the existing launcher, run-external-agent, and collect-agent-results contracts it claims to preserve. Look for mismatches in sidecar names, .meta/.done semantics, LAUNCHER_EXIT handling, add-dir defaults, retry reconstruction, timeout behavior, and foreground versus background callers. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: auth-scope-mapper
archetypes.rationale: The issue is about auth coverage drift, so a specialist should verify every planned Codex exec surface is actually swept and documented.
archetypes.prompt_body: Trace the repo evidence for all direct codex exec call sites named or implied by the issue, then compare that surface map to the plan's files, linter scope, and documentation updates. Focus on uncovered markdown fences, shell wrappers, negotiation flows, lint-fix flows, and any suppression rule that could accidentally bless an unsafe raw invocation. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: harness-contracts
archetypes.rationale: The plan relies heavily on new and extended harnesses, making test-plan adequacy and fixture realism a key defect risk.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review whether the proposed harnesses would actually detect the most likely implementation mistakes in this auth-launcher sweep. Check fixture realism, Bash 3.2 concerns, env-key versus login assertions, auth-prep failure simulation, stdout parsing of LAUNCHER_EXIT, pre-commit and Makefile shard coverage, and gaps between documented contracts and tested behavior. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
